correctness.rationale: The exact factorial-moment formula and hypergeometric coefficient transformation follow by counting uniform-subset avoidance. For nonpositive real-rooted input, mixed-half-plane nonvanishing of G(z,w) propagates to its w-derivatives by Gauss–Lucas; Hurwitz at w=0 is nontrivial by the binomial normalization at z=1. Thus the probability-generating polynomial remains real-rooted through every packet. Nonnegative coefficients force roots <=0; normalization yields Bernoulli factorization. Exchangeable polarization provides stable multiaffine generating polynomial. A standalone exact-rational program independently corroborates 710 distribution/root cases, 5144 factorial-moment identities, and eight subset enumerations; no finite experiment substitutes for infinite proof.

originality.rationale: Primary 2022 group-drawing analysis studies identical finite-vacancy observable but provides asymptotic bounds. General 2009/2023 real-stability and Poisson-binomial results supply consequences but do not imply that the successive uniform hypergeometric intersection update preserves real zeros without an additional theorem, which is proved in this result. An indexed 2012 sampling theorem concerns a different conditioned combination; its unread full text remains a residual priority risk.
residual_risks: Full Brändén–Jonasson 2012 text was unavailable, despite checking accessible author-indexed theorem and abstract; a broader uninspected closure result may subsume the claim.
Classical occupancy, real-stable polynomial and total-positivity literature could have an equivalent theorem in different terminology; failure to find one does not establish mathematical priority.

value.rationale: The number of unseen coupons in uniform group drawings is an established asymptotic statistical target (Betken–Thäle 2022 and Schilling–Henze 2021). The result determines, uniformly over arbitrary finite dimension, sample size, and heterogeneous packet sizes, an exact Poisson-binomial distributional structure together with a joint strongly Rayleigh law. This yields intrinsically useful exact finite-sample dependence and concentration information not supplied by Gaussian/Poisson limit approximations; it is not a parameter substitution or a finite census.
